version_guard.provenance: All four guarded probes ran against concrete Claude Code 2.1.307 on 2026-10-22; each ended version-guard: verdict=single-version start=2.1.307 end=2.1.307. Arm S observed concurrent hook execution in 12/12 event pairs with relay-first in 3/12. Arm D required three invocations: across 15 denied-scenario runs, 10 verified an errored Bash tool result and every completed run fired exactly one Stop, but 5 runs ended with the model declining to attempt the call (last messages like 'no Bash tool is available in this session' - a 2.1.307 model/deferred-tools shape, not a Stop-count finding: no completed run fired !=1 Stop); the arm's exit-1 ERROR is its scenario-coverage strictness, not a moved contract. Arm T killed all eight overrun firings while all four sessions exited 0 with replies, at 5.1-5.2 s after Stop-hook start. The dedicated TUI probe observed one Stop per turn at 9.4 s / 2.8 s. Arm P completed both sequential Bash rounds with --allowedTools=Bash, final message DONE, exit 0, one Stop; the allowed-tool TUI arm again did not complete its turns inside the driver window (zero firings, the incomplete-turn shape also seen on the 2.1.301 and 2.1.303 pins), so the tool-using TUI turn is measured by probe-claude-contracts T2 turn 1 (two Stops for two loaded sources) and the dedicated TUI probe. A same-session authenticated claude-print stream-json PTY capture used the same pinned binary; its 32-record stdout was byte-identical to the transcript, with no result, CR, or blank records. The capture newly observed a deferred_tools_delta attachment, and ai-title records occurred live again (twice; the 2.1.303 capture had none); auto_mode, date, and remote_session_change attachments flowed again. No tool-use or thinking record occurred; those cases remain retained from historical evidence. Replay bytes and error objects were produced and verified against the production reader and emitter.

notes.isolation: Every probe ran with HOME redirected into a throwaway sandbox; the host real settings and .claude.json were not read or modified. The host credentials file, when present, was copied file-to-file into the sandbox and never printed.
notes.cross_source_order_evidence: 2.1.307 Arm S: project hook sleeping 300 ms and relay hook 0 ms ran concurrently in 12/12 event pairs; the relay started first in 3/12. The result is concurrency, not a contractual source order: claude-print must not depend on order.
notes.tui_per_turn_evidence: The dedicated probe-tui-second-turn.sh run on 2.1.307 completed two TUI turns: turn 1 fired 1 Stop with its reply rendered in 9.4 s, and turn 2 fired 1 Stop with SECOND-OK rendered in 2.8 s. probe-claude-contracts T2 turn 1 (multi-round tool use, two loaded sources) fired two Stops - one per loaded source; its turn 2 did not complete inside the driver window (zero firings - the incomplete-turn re-run shape, not a rendered-reply-without-Stop finding). The allowed-tool TUI arm of probe-stop-toolallowed likewise produced zero firings inside its driver window; its Arm P print-mode contract passed: one Stop, DONE, exit 0. The per-turn TUI evidence for this pin is the dedicated probe.
notes.degraded_path_hazard: Arm D on 2.1.307 used a command-specific Bash deny rule and needed three invocations: 10 of 15 runs verified an errored Bash tool result, and every completed run - verified or not - exited 0 and fired exactly one Stop. The 5 unverified runs ended with the model declining the call ('no Bash tool is available in this session'), a 2.1.307 shape consistent with its new deferred-tools mechanism; it changes probe scenario coverage, not the Stop contract. The historical 2.1.270 extra-Stop hazard did not reproduce. The poller keeps first-payload tolerance for degraded runs.
notes.print_mode_tool_use_evidence: Arm P on 2.1.307 used --allowedTools=Bash in the isolated probe project. Both sequential Bash rounds completed in order, the final message was DONE, exit was 0, and exactly 1 Stop fired.
notes.cutoff_evidence: The focused 2.1.307 -p run with --max-turns 2 exited 1 and fired zero own Stops (the probe's per-arm print is the shared log's cumulative project count, 4, of which P1/P2/P6/T1 own one each); the cutoff remains owned by the --stop-hook-timeout watchdog, not the Stop Poller.
notes.hook_timeout_evidence: Arm T on 2.1.307 configured a relay-position hook with timeout 5 s and sleep 30 s: all 8 event firings were killed, all 4 sessions exited 0 with replies rendered, and each Stop hook-to-process completion was 5.1-5.2 s. This confirms the per-hook timeout field used by the relay.
